# API reference

Source of truth: the application's generated OpenAPI document (`/openapi.json`, interactive at `/docs`). On 2026-11-02 it listed
**42 paths / 46 operations** (generated by `app.openapi()` from `app.main:app`). This page was checked against that list and
against the route decorators in `app/api/v1/routes/*.py` and `app/api/simulation.py`.

## Conventions

* Base: `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. The root app serves `/health`, `/ready` and `/sim/*`; the versioned API is mounted at `/api/v1`.
* **Auth.** Every `/api/v1` route except `health` and `ready` needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The identity and roles come
  only from the verified token; no header or body field can name or elevate a user. With `APPROVAL_AUTH_MODE=disabled` (default)
  every token is rejected (`401 unauthenticated`).
* **Errors** have one shape: `{"error": {"code", "message", "request_id", "details"?}}`. Messages are fixed strings; validation
  details contain field names and rule names, never submitted values. Common codes: `unauthenticated` 401, `forbidden` 403,
  `not_found` 404, `conflict` 409, `validation_error` 422, `rate_limited` 429, `service_unavailable` 503, `recovery_unavailable` 503.
* The `/sim/*` routes on the root app are **unauthenticated** and read-only; for local development only.

## Roles and permissions (`app/api/v1/permissions.py`)

| Role | HTTP permissions |
|---|---|
| `viewer`, `api_reader` | `incident:read`, `investigation:read`, `approval:read`, `recovery:read`, `ticket:read`, `ledger:read` |
| `investigator` | read set (no ledger) + `incident:create`, `investigation:run` |
| `operator` | investigator + `recovery:request`, `recovery:resume`, `ticket:manage` |
| `recovery_approver`, `recovery_admin` | read set + `approval:decide` + `ledger:read` |
| `governance_authority` | none (re-enablement is deliberately not exposed over HTTP) |

`approval:decide` only reaches the decision endpoint. The approval service separately requires the per-action approver permission
(`recovery:approve:<action>`, `app/recovery/auth.py`) on every decision.

## Routes

### Health (open)

| Method and path | Notes |
|---|---|
| `GET /health`, `GET /api/v1/health` | Liveness |
| `GET /ready`, `GET /api/v1/ready` | Readiness and configuration state (for example the authentication mode); `/api/v1/ready` returns 503 `not_ready` when services cannot be built |

### Simulator

| Method and path | Auth |
|---|---|
| `GET /sim/db-status`, `/sim/pipelines`, `/sim/runs`, `/sim/runs/{run_id}`, `/sim/scenarios` | none, read-only |
| `GET /api/v1/simulator/pipelines`, `/runs`, `/incidents`, `/incidents/{incident_id}` | `incident:read` |
| `POST /api/v1/simulator/incidents/{incident_id}/import` | `incident:create`; 201 on first import, 200 if it already exists (idempotent) |

### Incidents and investigations

| Method and path | Auth / result |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/incidents` | `incident:create`; 201 (200 when an idempotent repeat) |
| `GET /api/v1/incidents`, `GET /api/v1/incidents/{incident_id}` | `incident:read` |
| `GET /api/v1/incidents/{incident_id}/status` | `incident:read`; derived workflow status (see below) |
| `POST /api/v1/incidents/{incident_id}/investigations` | `investigation:run`; **202**, runs as a background task |
| `GET /api/v1/incidents/{incident_id}/investigations`, `GET /api/v1/investigations/{investigation_id}`, `GET /api/v1/incidents/{incident_id}/report` | `investigation:read` |

Workflow status values include `approval_expired` (a pending approval past its expiry; see
[governance-and-safety.md](governance-and-safety.md#approval-lifecycle-and-expiry)). Starting an investigation never marks an
incident resolved.

### Recovery, reviews and approvals

| Method and path | Auth / result |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/incidents/{incident_id}/recoveries` | `recovery:request`; 202 (409 when blocked, for example a duplicate open claim); proposal only |
| `GET /api/v1/recoveries`, `GET /api/v1/incidents/{incident_id}/recoveries`, `GET /api/v1/recoveries/{recovery_id}` | `recovery:read` |
| `GET /api/v1/recoveries/{recovery_id}/governance` | `recovery:read`; governance view built from stored rows and ledger outcomes (lifecycle state, per-PreNode verdicts, request expiry) |
| `POST /api/v1/recoveries/{recovery_id}/resume` | `recovery:resume`; runs gates and, if everything holds, the action |
| `GET /api/v1/reviews`, `/reviews/summary`, `/reviews/{review_id}` | `approval:read`; only items genuinely waiting for a person |
| `GET /api/v1/approvals/{request_id}` | `approval:read`; `ApprovalOut` includes `status` (stored) and `effective_status` (stored status with expiry applied) |
| `POST /api/v1/approvals/{request_id}/decision` | `approval:decide` plus the per-action permission; expiry and binding enforced server-side |

When recovery is switched off (database not allow-listed / not `_test`), the recovery, review and approval routes answer
`503 recovery_unavailable`. This is the safety guard, not a fault.

### Tickets (optional GitHub Issues)

`POST /api/v1/incidents/{incident_id}/ticket` (201, or 200 if it exists) and `POST .../ticket/sync` need `ticket:manage`;
`GET .../ticket` needs `ticket:read`. Tested with fakes only.

### Ledger (read-only)

`GET /api/v1/ledger/summary`, `/events`, `/events/{entry_id}`, `/trace`, `/integrity`, `/audit` need `ledger:read`. The integrity
check verifies the hash chain inside one file and returns a checkpoint; it cannot detect tail truncation or replacement by an
older consistent chain without an external checkpoint.

### Demo and dashboard

`GET /api/v1/demo/summary`, `/demo/incidents`, `/demo/incidents/{incident_id}` (synthetic in-process `DEMO-nnnn` records, not
investigable) and `GET /api/v1/dashboard/summary` need `incident:read`.

## Verification level

Route behaviour is exercised by the offline tests (`tests/test_api_v1.py`, `test_api_e2e.py`, `test_phase11_openapi.py`,
`test_governance_view_api.py`, `test_approval_expiry_presentation.py`, and others) against in-memory fakes. The SQL Server-backed
paths and live HTTP behaviour on Windows were not exercised by this verification pass. Route names in this page match the
OpenAPI list above; per-route response schemas are in `/docs`.
